topic: A contract that needs three signatures in two countries — how long does that take your business right now?
format: Open with a specific failure moment — a real date, a real cost, a real consequence that feels immediately familiar to the reader
post:
A signed contract that should have taken 48 hours took 11 days.

The client was in Dubai. The department head was in Muscat. One signature was missing, then the wrong version got emailed, then someone printed and scanned a PDF that came back unreadable.

The deal didn't fall apart. But the relationship cooled.

If you're managing contracts across two countries through WhatsApp threads and email chains — you already know this feeling. The contract is done. The deal is agreed. But the paper still isn't signed.

For HR and finance managers handling employment contracts, offer letters, or service agreements across Oman and the GCC, this isn't a one-time problem. It's every month. Same friction. Different deal.
